module_title: Computer Architecture (CPU, ALU, CU) - Foundational Basics
introduction: Computer Architecture is a high-scoring topic in the 'Computer Knowledge' section of competitive exams (SSC, Banking, Railways). At this foundational level, we focus on understanding the 'Brain of the Computer' (the CPU) and its three primary internal components: the ALU, the CU, and Registers.

core_concepts.title: CPU (Central Processing Unit)
core_concepts.description: Referred to as the 'Brain of the Computer'. It is responsible for processing all instructions received from hardware and software. A microprocessor is essentially a CPU built onto a single integrated circuit (IC) chip.

core_concepts.title: ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit)
core_concepts.description: The component of the CPU that actually performs the physical work. It handles all Arithmetic operations (Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, Division) and Logical operations (Comparing data like Greater Than, Less Than, or Equal To).

core_concepts.title: CU (Control Unit)
core_concepts.description: Often called the 'Nervous System' or 'Manager' of the computer. The CU does not perform any actual calculations. Instead, it directs the flow of data between the CPU, memory, and input/output devices, telling them how to respond to program instructions.

core_concepts.title: Registers (Memory Unit)
core_concepts.description: Registers are tiny, ultra-fast storage locations built directly inside the CPU. They temporarily hold the data and instructions that the ALU needs immediately to perform a calculation.

important_entities.name: John von Neumann
important_entities.significance: Introduced the 'Stored Program Concept' in 1945, which dictates that both data and instructions should be stored in the same memory space.

important_entities.name: Motherboard
important_entities.significance: The primary printed circuit board (PCB) that holds and connects the CPU, memory, and all peripheral connectors together.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants frequently mistake the Hard Disk (HDD/SSD) as part of the CPU. The CPU strictly consists of only the ALU, CU, and Registers. Everything else is secondary storage or a peripheral device.
Remember that the Control Unit (CU) never processes data or performs math. It strictly acts as a traffic cop, routing data to the ALU where the actual calculation happens.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember the three core internal components of a CPU, remember that it operates using its 'CAR': Control Unit, Arithmetic Logic Unit, and Registers.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct questions asking for the full forms of ALU and CU are staples in basic tier-1 exams (like IBPS Clerk or SSC CHSL). Memorize them flawlessly.
